preconditionEvidence: Atlas UX Agent State BLOCKED revision 3
observations: Activation model supports settled prior execution statuses RESULT_SUBMITTED and BLOCKED and requires Agent-owned rearm before next claim.
Runtime validate_agent_state_rearm_transition validates BLOCKED -> WAITING_HUMAN_GO after terminal MASTER resolution and typed blocking response.
The only rearm state template in the Framework was agent-state-reidentification-ready.template.json.
That template explicitly requires prior runtimeStatus REIDENTIFICATION_REQUIRED.
Agent Job schema did not bind a distinct settled-execution rearm template.
Publishing Job 011 safely would therefore require free-form state construction or misuse of a contradictory template.
verdictReason: FAIL: rc.6 allowed BLOCKED settled-execution rearm in the activation/runtime contract but had no separately bound state-construction template. The only existing rearm template was explicitly restricted to prior REIDENTIFICATION_REQUIRED. Publishing Job 011 would therefore require free-form or semantically contradictory state construction.
rootCause: The BLOCKED/RESULT_SUBMITTED rearm lifecycle was added to runtime and activation semantics without adding a separate immutable state-construction template and mandatory Job binding for that transition.
learnedRule: Every authoritative Agent-State transition that an LLM must materialize must have a distinct exact template bound by the active Job whenever its semantic preconditions differ; runtime support alone is insufficient.
